learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: In the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus showed that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, which is the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term do researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper use to describe the tendency to forget information once it has been saved digitally?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper call the tendency to forget information once it's offloaded to a device 'Digital Amnesia' — the brain treats saving something as permission to stop remembering it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In Scrum, which artifact is a visual chart that shows the remaining work in a Sprint and helps track whether the team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is one of Scrum's three artifacts; it visualizes a Sprint's progress and shows how much work remains so the team can track whether it's on schedule.

learnings.question: What is the primary reason Scrum breaks a project into short, iterative cycles called Sprints?
options: To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To increase the overall length of the project
To eliminate the need for meetings
To reduce the number of team members needed
learnings.learning: Scrum's core purpose for using short, iterative Sprints is to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments rather than committing to one long, rigid plan.

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what Arabic term refers to humanity's role as a steward or caretaker of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Khalifah is the term for humanity's role as caretaker of the Earth, a responsibility that includes preserving faith and fostering unity within the community.

learnings.question: In the Quran, what reason is given for why God created death and life?
options: To establish the Day of Judgment
To test which of you is best in deed
learnings.learning: Quran 67:2 states that God created death and life specifically to test people as to which of them is best in deed, framing earthly life as a test of conduct.

learnings.question: Per a common Islamic framework describing human purpose, which three roles define a person's life on Earth?
options: Worshiping God, acting as steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter
Following law, pursuing happiness, and avoiding sin
Gaining knowledge, building wealth, and achieving fame
Seeking wealth, raising a family, and serving the community
learnings.learning: A common framework for human purpose in Islam centers on three roles: worshiping Allah, serving as khalifah (steward) of the Earth, and preparing for the eternal Hereafter through accountability.

learnings.question: Which PCIe power management state is described as a very light sleep mode meant for only brief periods of idleness, letting the link wake almost instantly?
learnings.learning: L0s is PCIe's lightest power-saving state, comparable to a screen turning off — the link can wake quickly and it's designed only for very short idle periods.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state offers the greatest power savings but takes the longest time to resume activity, comparable to a computer being completely shut down?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, almost completely powering down the device — it delivers the highest power savings but has the longest wake-up time, much like a full shutdown.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to Allah's complete and eternal foreknowledge of everything that will happen, as distinct from the events as they actually unfold?
learnings.learning: Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal plan and foreknowledge of all events, while Qada' refers to how those events actually unfold in a person's life.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11 is frequently cited in Islamic teaching to support which idea?
options: People's own actions can change their circumstances
Prayer is unnecessary since all is predestined
Only prophets can alter their destiny
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11 — 'Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves' — is used to show that a person's own actions and choices can change their circumstances (Qada').
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: What practical action does the Qada' and Qadr teaching encourage believers to take, despite everything already being known to God?
options: Accept all outcomes passively without effort
Make sincere Dua (supplication) and strive for positive change
learnings.learning: Even though Allah already knows everything within Qadr, believers are encouraged to make sincere Dua and actively strive for positive change, since that effort is itself part of the divine plan.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Roughly what ratio of distinct Arabic words to English words (per the Oxford English Dictionary) is cited when comparing the vocabulary sizes of the two languages?
learnings.learning: With roughly 12 million distinct Arabic words versus about 170,000 English words in the Oxford English Dictionary, the cited ratio is approximately 71 Arabic words for every 1 English word.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What is the term for the small diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the small markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds; without them, reading Arabic text accurately becomes much harder.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: When the Pareto Principle (80/20 rule) was tested against word frequency in the Quran, what share of the total text did the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Testing the Pareto Principle against the Quran's word frequency showed the top 20 most repeated words account for only about 20.83% of the text, not the 80% the 80/20 rule might suggest.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
